extra.message: SQL injection in GET /select: the user-controlled query parameter 'username' is interpolated directly into the f-string f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";' and passed to run_sql_query(), which executes it via aiosqlite db.execute() with no parameterization (main.py:146). An attacker can supply username=" OR 1=1; -- to return every user record or inject arbitrary SQL.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: SQL injection in PUT /user: all user-controlled fields of the User model (name, username, password, address, email, contact) are interpolated via an f-string into the INSERT statement (main.py:188-203) and executed by run_sql_query without parameterization. A crafted field such as name="x"); DROP TABLE users;-- allows arbitrary SQL execution.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: SQL injection in DELETE /user: the user-supplied 'username' query parameter is interpolated into f'DELETE FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";' and executed by run_sql_query with no parameterization. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. username=" OR 1=1; --) to delete all rows or run other statements.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: SQL injection in DELETE /user: the user-controlled 'address' field is interpolated unquoted into f'DELETE FROM users WHERE address = {user.address};' and executed without parameterization. An attacker controls address in the JSON body and can inject arbitrary SQL tokens (e.g. address=1 OR 1=1).

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: NoSQL injection in POST /find: the raw request body JSON is parsed and passed unfiltered to get_nosql_users(), which executes users.find(query) (main.py:171). An attacker can send query operators such as {"id":{"$in":[1,2]}} or {"$where":"..."} to bypass the intended username filter and exfiltrate the entire collection. The endpoint also has no authentication.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: Missing authentication on GET /select: the endpoint returns arbitrary user records (name, username, address, email, contact) for any supplied username with no authentication or authorization check anywhere in the application (no security dependency, no auth middleware). Any unauthenticated client can enumerate and read all stored PII.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Missing authentication on GET /find (and POST /find): user records are returned based on a caller-supplied username/query with no authentication or authorization. Any unauthenticated client can read arbitrary user PII from the NoSQL collection.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Missing authentication/authorization on PUT /user: any unauthenticated caller can create user records in both SQLite and the NoSQL store, including setting arbitrary usernames and passwords. There is no credential or role check protecting this state-changing operation.

Broken access control / IDOR on DELETE /user: the endpoint deletes any user record identified by the caller-supplied 'username' query parameter (or by 'address' in the body) with no authentication and no ownership/authorization check. Any unauthenticated attacker can delete other users' records.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Missing authentication on POST /reset: an unauthenticated request deletes the SQLite database file and the NoSQL store directory and reinitializes the data (main.py:244-246), causing complete data loss and denial of service. This critical destructive function has no authentication or authorization.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (md5(user.password.encode()).hexdigest(), main.py:187; also used for seeded data at main.py:113). MD5 is cryptographically broken, fast to brute-force, and lacks salting, so stored password hashes can be cracked or reversed via rainbow tables.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Sensitive data exposure in run_sql_query: when a query returns more than one row, the raw fetchall() rows are returned as {'users': _data}, which includes the password column (index 3) selected by 'SELECT *'. The single-row path strips the password, but the multi-row path leaks password hashes. This is directly reachable through the SQL-injectable GET /select endpoint.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
